readings.R1: Fiber samples (4.1): the controlled polyline (each control point is anchored at its nearest line point; the span runs from the smallest to the largest anchor index, as tools/fibers_json_to_afv.py), in sv (level 0 / 4), sampled at arclength 0, 1, 2, ... sv and at its end. (The frozen plan's stretches S0105, S0117 and S0770 end at their fibers' non-integer lengths, so the end sample exists.)
readings.R2: "Distance to its fiber" (the 30 sv row window and the 5 sv association median, 5.2) is the distance from the row centre to the nearest fiber sample, the sample that also gives the row's arclength. (The distance to the polyline would be smaller by at most 0.5 sv at 0 sv, 0.025 sv at 5 sv, 0.004 sv at 30 sv.)
readings.R3: Every bound is inclusive on the accepted side: a row centre exactly 30 sv from its fiber is scored, a strip node exactly 30 sv from the crossing point counts, |d| = 30 sv and a sideways residual of exactly 1 sv are covered, a median centre distance of exactly 5 sv is associated, a V sample exactly 6 sv away counts, and |d| = 1 or 2 sv is within 1 or 2 sv.
readings.R4: The row centre is the node of column C // 2 (25 columns: column 12, v = 0), or the mean of the row's valid nodes when that node is invalid. For an even C the column C // 2 is used and a note is written.
readings.R5: The association median is over every row that has a centre (at least one valid node). A rejected strip (median above 5 sv) scores no row.
readings.R6: "Falls inside a matched stretch": s0 <= s <= s1 for the arclength s of the row's nearest sample, for any stretch of the strip's fiber in the scored set (secondary: run = true; primary: both), on that fiber's whole controlled span. Rows that fall in a stretch of another piece are counted (rows_in_other_pieces_stretches); a row in two stretches takes the first id (listed in rows_in_two_stretches). Other reading, reported (own_windows_only): only the stretches of the piece's own windows. Five fibers of the sample have two run pieces (P0005/P0006, P0083/P0084, P0125/P0126, P0149/P0150, P0179/P0180), where the readings can differ.
readings.R7: Projection (5.1). PREREG names Gauss-Newton from the 4 nearest nodes, not its iterations, step control or behaviour at cell edges. Here the foot is the closest point of the bilinear surface of the valid cells (cells whose 4 corners are valid) that lie within two cells of the point's 4 nearest valid nodes; per cell it is found by Gauss-Newton inside the cell and exactly on the cell's 4 straight edges. The normal is the surface normal at the foot (cross product of the two grid derivatives), d = (p - foot) . n, and the sideways residual is the part of p - foot orthogonal to n. A point is covered when a foot exists, the sideways residual is <= 1 sv and |d| <= 30 sv. A foot on a cell edge or node (a crease) has one normal per valid cell there: the one that fits p - foot best (the smallest sideways residual) gives d, and d and the sideways residual over all of them are kept for tier 2.
readings.R8: "Positive outward (away from the umbilicus)": per point, n is turned so that its horizontal part points away from the umbilicus at the foot's z (the umbilicus linear in z between its control points, constant beyond them: the scorer's rule, see INDEPENDENCE). Without an umbilicus (crossings, the Paris 4 fixture) only |d| is used.
readings.R9: Statistics are over the covered nodes of scored rows: mean, median and p90 (numpy's linear percentile) of |d|, the fraction with |d| <= 1 and <= 2 sv, the signed mean of d. The fiber floor (5.6) is, per scored row, |d| of the fiber sample that gives the row's arclength, on the same segment; fiber_floor_mean_abs_sv is its mean over the scored rows where that sample is covered. (The per-piece aggregation is the scorer's, see INDEPENDENCE.)
readings.R10: The fiber rule of 5.2 (fewer than 25 covered nodes: not scored) applies to pooled numbers only; per-piece and per-stretch numbers are reported for every strip that is not rejected.
readings.R11: Crossing point (7): for every sample of the H fiber the nearest sample of any V fiber of the scroll (k = 1; family from the JSON tag, manual if H or V, else automatic) is taken if within 6 sv; among the H samples whose nearest is on the crossing's V fiber the closest gives the point, the midpoint of that H sample and its nearest V sample. The recomputed point, not the plan's, is used for the agreement; both are reported.
readings.R12: Crossing strips: the strips of the pieces that hold the crossing's H and V windows in the plan. Each must run along its piece's own fiber (5.2: median centre distance, R2, R4, R5, <= 5 sv); a strip that does not is rejected and the crossing is missing (7: planned crossings without both strips are listed as missing). The association medians are reported. "Nodes within 30 sv of the crossing point": valid strip nodes at Euclidean distance <= 30 sv. "Covered by the other strip": covered as in R7 on the other strip's surface, unsigned. The median is over those covered nodes. Other reading, reported (other_reading): each strip belongs to the planned fiber it runs closest to (median <= 5 sv), and per fiber the strip with the most valid nodes within 30 sv of the point is used.

tolerance.text: existed but without reading them, because a review showed that tier 1 alone calls a correct scorer different when strips lie far off the mesh) Tier 1, 'agree': integers (node counts, numbers of usable directions, missing status, a piece's stretch ids, numbers of scored fibers, sample counts, and the fractions within 1 and 2 sv, compared as node counts) exactly; values in sv (means, medians, p90, max, fiber floor, association median, agreement, crossing point and closest approach) within 1e-3 sv. Both codes read the same float32 coordinates and compute in float64; when both find the same foot a distance agrees to about 1e-9 sv, while another surface model (planar facets, nearest-node planes) moves it by up to the facet sagitta, about 0.02 sv (PREREG 8). 1e-3 sv is 1/1500 of the 1.5 sv gate and below the 2-decimal precision of the reported numbers. Why a tier 2: PREREG 5.1 names the method, not its iterations, step control or behaviour at cell edges, so the scorer and R7 are two solvers of one definition. Near the mesh they find the same foot. Far from it the distance has several local minima, at a crease the normal is not unique, and near the 1 sv and 30 sv bounds a small change flips coverage: there two correct solvers differ in coverage and in |d|. (The review measured, on synthetic meshes, node counts off by up to 5 % and means by up to 0.40 sv for strips tilted 10 to 40 deg or on a mesh with 0.3 sv node noise, |d| differences up to 0.64 sv at 12 to 30 sv, and crossing agreements off by 0.03 to 0.79 sv; good strips agreed within 2.6e-4 sv.) Classes (classify(); d and the sideways residual are taken over every normal at the foot, R7): robust: covered, |d| <= 6 sv and sideways residual <= 0.5 sv for every normal at the foot, and |d| varying by at most 1e-3 sv between them (6 sv: half a winding gap, the NF6 window of PREREG 4.4; 0.5 sv: half the coverage bound); sensitive: any other node whose foot another solver may cover. Its |d| can be <= 30 sv: least - delta_below <= 30 sv, where least = sqrt(distance^2 - 1 sv^2) is the smallest |d| a covering foot can give (no foot is nearer than this file's closest point, and a covering one is at most 1 sv sideways). And either its foot lies inside the mesh (on a crease or node there the residual depends on the normal), or on the mesh edge with a sideways residual <= max(1.5 sv, 0.35 x the distance) (far from the mesh another solver can find an inner local minimum); firmly uncovered: the rest (no foot; |d| out of reach; a foot on the mesh edge with a larger residual). Tier 2 tests this hypothesis: the scorer gives every robust node this file's |d| within 0.005 sv + 2 % of |d|, covers no firmly uncovered node, and covers any subset of the sensitive nodes, each with |d| in [least - delta_below, distance + delta_above] (delta_below = 0.1 sv + 2 % of the distance: a closest point that this file's cells could miss; delta_above = 0.1 sv + 10 % of the distance: another local minimum farther away) and d on the node's side of the mesh (either side when the normals at the foot disagree). Every compared value then has an interval: the count of covered nodes; a mean or signed mean (the scorer's node count fixes how many sensitive nodes it covers, and the interval runs from that many smallest lower bounds to that many largest upper bounds); median, p90 and max; the within-1 and within-2 counts; the fiber floor and the crossing medians (over every count, since the scorer does not report it; for a crossing direction every count the 5-node rule allows); the 25-node rule; the number of usable directions. Tier 2, 'agree_within_solver_bounds': every value that fails tier 1 lies in its interval, widened by the tier-1 tolerance. Values that do not depend on the projection must pass tier 1: the association median, the crossing point and closest approach, the sample count of the ground-truth check, a missing or rejected strip. Each interval is written with its width, which is what the item could still detect: a wide interval means the item cannot tell a defect from a solver difference. 'agree_under_other_reading': the item passes tier 1 or 2 only under R6's or R12's other reading. 'differs': none of these; neither the solver nor a flagged reading explains the difference. The thresholds were set from the geometry above and revised twice, before any comparison with the run's reports (which existed by then but were not read), after checks against the frozen scorer run as a black box (the review's scripts; 116,000 points on synthetic cylinders of radius 60 and 300 sv with node noise 0 to 0.3 sv, with and without holes, and on 4 Paris 4 G0 strips as surfaces, up to 35 sv off the mesh; no PHerc0139 or PHerc0332 data). The first check found 369 nodes this file called firmly uncovered that the scorer covered, far off noisy meshes (54 still so after the inner-crease rule, all with the foot on the mesh edge), 5 robust nodes off by 0.007 to 0.026 sv, and 3 sensitive nodes up to 0.19 sv outside their interval. Hence the inner-crease rule, the edge residual of 0.35 x the distance, the relative allowances and the asymmetric delta. With the final rules no point of those checks violates them (worst robust difference 0.026 sv; scorer feet up to 6.9 % of the distance farther than the closest point; covered edge feet with residuals up to 0.21 x the distance). A later out-of-sample review on other shapes (folds, wrinkles, a spiral turn of more than 360 deg, sphere caps, ragged and collapsed edges; 54,000 points) found points outside these rules: 42 of 13,424 robust nodes outside the allowance and 1 robust node uncovered (all on wrinkled meshes), 19 firmly uncovered nodes that the scorer covered (8 on wrinkled meshes, 11 on the spiral turn: its local solver stopped on another wrinkle or layer, farther than the closest point), 574 sensitive nodes outside their interval and 2 with the wrong sign on a 90 deg fold; and, on wrinkled meshes, 1 false 'differs' of the ground-truth check in 295 to 620 stretches (a median |d| 0.003 sv outside its interval). Whole pieces still agreed or agreed within the bounds (27 of 27). So a ground-truth 'differs' of a few thousandths of a sv on a wrinkled mesh, or scorer coverage of nodes this file calls firmly uncovered where another layer or wrinkle is within reach, can be a solver difference. On the first review's 42 per-piece cases 27 agree and 15 agree within the solver bounds: the mean's interval is 0.07 to 0.23 sv wide on good strips and up to 8.3 sv on strips tilted 40 deg. Of its 8 crossings, 3 agree and 5 agree within the bounds. Its three edge cases agree: a strip with no row in a window, a crossing strip 8 sv off its fiber, and no primary fiber scored.
